questions.question: What does @Async do to a method?
options: Runs it on a separate thread so the caller does not wait
Runs it inside a database transaction
questions.explanation: @Async hands the call to a task executor, so the caller carries on while the method runs in the background.

questions.question: Which return types are normal for an @Async method?
questions.explanation: The caller cannot get a plain value from a background call. void means fire and forget, and CompletableFuture carries the answer later.

questions.question: Two @Async methods each sleep 1 second. A caller starts both and then waits for both with join(). About how long does it take?
questions.explanation: The two methods run on different pool threads at the same time, so the total is close to the longest one, 1 second.

questions.question: With Spring Boot's default async executor, what does Thread.currentThread().getName() usually start with inside an @Async method?
questions.explanation: Boot names the threads of its default task executor with the prefix task-.

questions.question: A service has @Async void sendMail() and another method in the same class calls this.sendMail(). The caller still waits. Why?
options: The call inside the same class skips the proxy, so it runs synchronously
questions.explanation: @Async works through a proxy. A call from inside the same object does not pass through it, so nothing becomes async.
